newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - Guardian, Allianz and rates.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - Guardian, Allianz and rates.

text.p: British insurer Guardian and its shareholders will have breathed a sigh of relief this morning at the positive reaction to its 1996 results. Trading profits were down on 1995, but in line with expectations at this stage in the insurance cycle.

Guardian, formerly GRE, is the smallest of Britain's big four quoted insurers and traditionally is the first to unveil its annual results. Its comments on market pricing trends set the scene for the results season as a whole and can carry disproportionate weight. In recent years, this has sometimes led to problems for the sector as a whole, as news hungry observers have sent shares plunging on the slightest hint that rates may be headed south.

This year, Guardian made clear that it expects motor rates to build on last year's gentle firming trend, while household rates should stop falling and may even start climbing. Commercial rates, which lag moves in personal lines, remain competitive.
Commercial Union will give its opinion on rating trends with its results tomorrow, but is unlikely to have had a markedly different experience to Guardian.
Guardian also commented on the German non-life market, where it is represented by its Albingia unit, describing conditions as difficult.
More importantly, German market leader Allianz issued its results and forecast for 1997, warning of a downturn in non-life premium income.

In the past, the market had to wait much longer for Allianz's results and views on the year ahead. This year, the company has brought forward its results in a spirit of glasnost and under pressure from investors.

However, Allianz was upbeat about profits in the current year, forecasting an increase thanks to tighter cost and claims controls. In mature non-life markets such as Germany and Britain, lowering costs will remain at the core of insurers' strategies to maintain or improve profits. Underpinning this will be the process of industry consolidation, which still offers the best opportunities to reduce prices in the long term.
